title: Nested objects and arrays
learningObjectives: Explain nested objects and arrays and read or transform JavaScript data safely.

understand.concept: Objects can contain other objects and arrays, creating nested data structures. Access nested values with chained dot or bracket notation. Check each level when data may be missing, or use optional chaining to avoid errors on nullish intermediate values.
understand.whyItMatters: Nested data is common in API responses and application state. Deeply nested structures can become difficult to maintain, so use clear schemas and safe access patterns.
understand.analogy: A nested object is like a folder containing other folders and files; each level must exist before you open the next.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript references, serialization, and DOM APIs have precise behaviour defined by the language and web platform.

explain.narrative: The course object contains an array of lesson objects. The code reads a nested property and a boolean state.

examples.explanation: The course object contains an array of lesson objects. The code reads a nested property and a boolean state.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page displays the selected, transformed, or serialized data.

practise.guidedTask: Create a nested course object with modules and lessons. Access one lesson's title and completion state safely.
practise.independentTask: Build a small data-processing or DOM-selection example. Include missing-data handling and explain any shallow-copy or serialization limits.
hints: Check optional properties before accessing them.
Remember shallow copies share nested references.
Handle JSON parsing errors and validate data shape.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Nested objects and arrays</title></head><body>
<script>const course={title:'Web Basics',lessons:[{name:'HTML',done:true},{name:'CSS',done:false}]};console.log(course.lessons[0].name,course.lessons[1].done);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: How do you access the first lesson name in the example structure?
questions.explanation: The lessons property is an array; index zero is its first object, whose name property is read.

questions.prompt: What is a safe approach when working with nested or external data?
options: Check structure and handle missing or invalid values
Use JSON parsing as schema validation
questions.answer: Check structure and handle missing or invalid values
questions.explanation: External data must be checked for expected shape and valid values.
